parts.label: (a)
parts.official_mark_scheme_text: Factorise the left side as a difference of two squares. [*M1] Simplify using $\cos^2\theta+\sin^2\theta=1$, which must be seen or implied. [DM1] Obtain the given identity from correct working. [A1 AG] The printed alternatives using rearranged double-angle formulae or Pythagoras earn the same dependent marks. Total: 3.

parts.label: (b)
parts.official_mark_scheme_text: Use part (a) and the correct double-angle formula to rewrite the integrand in terms of $\cos2\theta$ and $\sin^22\theta$ (or $\cos^22\theta$); allow BOD for $2\sin^22\theta$ only when $\sin2\theta=2\sin\theta\cos\theta$ is seen. [M1] Use or imply $\int\cos2\theta\,d\theta=\frac12\sin2\theta$. [B1] Use the correct double-angle formula on the second term to obtain a directly integrable form, e.g. $\int\sin^22\theta\,d\theta=\int(1-\cos4\theta)/2\,d\theta$. [M1] Obtain $\frac12\sin2\theta+\frac12\theta-\frac18\sin4\theta$. [A1] Apply limits $\pm\pi/8$ correctly and evaluate the trigonometric values. [M1] Obtain $\frac{\sqrt2}{2}+\frac\pi8-\frac14$, or exact equivalent from exact working; ISW. [A1] Total: 6.
